promptText: Linear vs Monday, which one should I choose?
rawText:
The choice between **Linear** and **Monday.com** comes down to one fundamental question: **Are you building software, or are you managing general business operations?**

Here is the quick answer (TL;DR), followed by a detailed breakdown:

*   **Choose Linear** if you are a software development, product, or engineering team that wants a lightning-fast, highly opinionated tool optimized for building software (a modern alternative to Jira).
*   **Choose Monday.com** if you are a non-technical team (marketing, sales, HR, operations) or a whole company that needs a flexible, highly customizable "Work OS" to manage diverse projects and processes.

---

### Detailed Comparison

| Feature / Aspect | **Linear** | **Monday.com** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Focus** | Software development, issue tracking, product roadmaps. | General project management, operations, marketing, CRM. |
| **User Target** | Developers, Product Managers, Designers. | Cross-functional teams, Marketing, Ops, HR, Executives. |
| **Philosophy** | **Opinionated & Streamlined:** Built to fit standard tech workflows out of the box. | **Customizable & Flexible:** Build whatever system you want using building blocks. |
| **Speed & Performance** | **Ultra-fast:** Keyboard-centric, zero lag, designed for developer efficiency. | Moderate: Feature-dense and visual, but can feel slower. |
| **Customization** | Low to Moderate (Keeps the UI clean and structured). | High (Custom fields, views, column types, dashboards). |
| **Key Integrations** | GitHub, GitLab, Figma, Sentry, Slack, LaunchDarkly. | Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Google Workspace, Zapier. |
| **Learning Curve** | Extremely low for software teams. | Low for basic use, but steep to set up complex automations. |

---

### Deep Dive: Linear

Linear was designed specifically to solve the frustration software engineers have with slow, bloated tools like Jira.

#### **Why choose Linear?**
1. **Speed & UX:** It is arguably the fastest project management tool available. It heavily relies on keyboard shortcuts (Cmd/Ctrl + K menu) so developers rarely have to touch the mouse.
2. **Built for Modern Dev Workflows:** It automatically syncs with GitHub/GitLab. When a developer creates a pull request or merges code, Linear automatically updates the issue status.
3. **Opinionated System:** Linear enforces good habits (Cycles/Sprints, Triage, Backlogs, Roadmaps). You spend zero time configuring custom fields and more time shipping code.
4. **Clean Design:** Minimalist, modern dark-mode aesthetic that tech teams love.

#### **When NOT to use Linear:**
* You have non-technical departments (e.g., Marketing, Legal, HR) who need to track their work—Linear will feel too rigid or technical for them.
* You need complex budget tracking, Gantt chart resource allocation, or custom CRM capabilities.

---

### Deep Dive: Monday.com

Monday.com is a visual "Work OS" designed to adapt to almost any business use case across an entire enterprise.

#### **Why choose Monday.com?**
1. **Extreme Versatility:** You can use Monday as a project tracker, a sales CRM, a content calendar, an HR onboarding pipeline, or event planner.
2. **Visual & Intuitive:** Uses color-coded statuses, drag-and-drop interfaces, Kanban boards, Gantt charts, and timeline views that make high-level project status easy for managers and clients to understand.
3. **Powerful Automations:** You can easily build "If this, then that" automations (e.g., *"When a status changes to 'Done', notify the manager and move item to Board B"*).
4. **Cross-Departmental Unity:** Marketing, Sales, and Ops can all work in the same platform using interconnected boards.

#### **When NOT to use Monday.com:**
* You are a pure engineering team. Monday lacks deep, native git-level integration out of the box compared to Linear, and setting up agile sprint management requires tedious manual configuration.
* You want a fast, lightweight interface. Monday can feel cluttered and slow if over-configured.

---

### Pricing Comparison

* **Linear:** Offers a generous **Free tier** (up to 250 active issues). Paid plans start around **$8 to $12 per user/month**. Very transparent.
* **Monday.com:** Has a limited Free tier (2 users max). Paid plans start around **$9 to $19+ per user/month** (billed annually), but note that Monday sells seats in **minimum seat blocks** (e.g., 3, 5, 10 seats), which can make it pricier for small teams.

---

### Final Decision Guide

**Choose Linear if:**
* You are a startup founder, software engineer, or tech product manager.
* Your main goal is tracking bugs, feature requests, sprints, and code releases.
* You hate bloat and value speed/keyboard navigation.

**Choose Monday.com if:**
* You run an agency, marketing team, operations department, or non-tech business.
* You need client-facing dashboards or high-level visual reporting for executives.
* You want **one platform** to manage the entire company's non-dev operations.
